name: Aurobindo Pharma Ltd

profile.text: Hyderabad-based maker of generic medicines and APIs, founded 1986 by P.V. Ramprasad Reddy and K. Nithyananda Reddy; IPO 1992. Largest Indian generics supplier to the US by approved ANDAs (737 final approvals, 896 filed at Jun-2026). 30+ manufacturing facilities (18 commercial FDF units, 13 API units), 6 R&D centres, exports to 150+ countries; 20+ facilities US FDA and EU GMP approved.
profile.src: AR FY26 pp.6-7; Q1FY27 presentation p.21

fy26.src: Q4FY26 presentation and call (22-May-2026); AR FY26 notes 24, 25, 35

guidance.said: EBITDA margin on the higher side of 20-21% for FY26
No major greenfield beyond biologics; capex not beyond ~$150-200mn a year plus $80-120mn for the biologics CMO over two years
EBITDA margin to sustain and progressively improve to north of 21%
Heading towards a $2bn US business 'maybe in the next 1-2 years', Lannett (~$300mn) part of it; no 'big bang' acquisition
China plant to turn EBITDA positive in FY27 (FY26 loss ~$7mn), low double-digit margin targeted; Pen-G and 6-APA lost Rs200 cr+ of EBITDA in FY26 but turned positive in Q4FY26
guidance.outcome: China output doubled in a year; Pen-G at 800-900 t a month

guidance.said: Double-digit revenue growth, EBITDA margin north of 21%, absolute EBITDA above Rs8,000 cr, with upside from strategic businesses
guidance.outcome: Reiterated after Q1 (Rs1,924 cr operating EBITDA)

guidance.said: Single-digit growth in FY27, ~$500mn+ revenue, because Unit III cannot get new approvals; remediation with consultants
guidance.outcome: Unit I warning letter followed on 13-Aug-2026

guidance.said: Double-digit growth in FY27; Europe EBITDA margin has crossed 20%
R&D Rs1,450-1,500 cr in FY27 (biosimilar phase-3 studies done); tax rate to normalise to 28-29% by year-end (31.9% in Q1)
Asked whether EBITDA reaches Rs2,200 cr a quarter from Q2: 'that is what our objective and target is', subject to the Middle East situation

deals.terms: US$250mn (Rs2,185 cr at signing) cash-free, debt-free incl. normalised working capital; US$247mn paid in Q1FY27. Agreed 30-Jul-2025; FTC cleared 18-Jun-2026 on condition of divesting four products (mycophenolate oral suspension, niacin ER, pilocarpine, rabeprazole) to Quagen
deals.economics: Net sales US$314mn (FY23), US$286mn (FY24), US$306mn (TTM FY25, June year-end); Seymour, Indiana plant (~3.6-4bn doses a year) at ~40% utilisation; controlled substances (ADHD), DEA quotas; gAdvair launch planned for Aug-2026. Management: ~US$60mn a quarter base sales before new products; SG&A, procurement and utilisation synergies over 9-12 months
deals.src: NSE filing 30-Jul-2025; FTC press release 18-Jun-2026; Business Today 22-Jun-2026; Q1FY27 call

deals.terms: Rs325 cr cash (slump sale, subject to working-capital true-up); ~US$32mn paid in Q4FY26
deals.economics: 23 brands, 67 SKUs, 9 pipeline products (anti-infectives, pain); FY25 revenue Rs113.5 cr, EBITDA Rs29.0 cr
deals.src: Exchange filing 1-Jan-2026 (Business Standard, Angel One); Q4FY26 presentation

deals.status: Agreed Jul-2026; closing expected within 1-2 months of the Q1 call
deals.terms: Enterprise value US$17mn; Apitoria pays US$13.6mn for 80%
deals.economics: Revenue Rs106 cr (FY25), Rs102 cr (FY26); 50+ customers; to become an integrated CRDMO with Aurobindo's API plants

regulatory.impact: EBITDA loss ~US$7mn in FY26; positive expected in FY27; supplies Europe and, from Q2FY27, the US

biosimilars.approved: Dyrupeg (pegfilgrastim: EMA, MHRA, Health Canada), Zefylti (filgrastim: EMA, MHRA), Bevqolva (bevacizumab: MHRA, Health Canada, CDSCO), Dazublys (trastuzumab: EMA, MHRA, CDSCO); all four now supplied commercially in the UK; rollout in seven EU countries; tenders in Mexico
biosimilars.filed: Denosumab (Filvizy / Fugevy) with EMA and CDSCO; omalizumab EMA filing due Q3 2026; first US filings (omalizumab, denosumab, bevacizumab) 'imminent'
biosimilars.later: Tocilizumab (filing 2027), ranibizumab (phase 3), trastuzumab SC (phase 1 in 2026), next wave of eight products (2030+)
biosimilars.partners: STADA (two EMA-approved biosimilars, France/Germany), Orion (Nordics), partners in Algeria, Uzbekistan, Mexico
biosimilars.investment: ~US$450mn of capex and opex in biosimilars since Jul-2018 (CEO, 22-May-2026); 10,000 L of new bioreactors being added
biosimilars.guidance: 7-8 products in EU, UK and Canada by 2028-29; at least three in the US by 2030; gross margin ~65% after price erosion
biosimilars.src: Q4FY26 and Q1FY27 presentations and calls

theranym.text: Biologics contract manufacturer (CMO) anchored by Merck Sharp & Dohme: first product schedule signed 29-May-2024, second in FY26, third (Unit 2) in Apr-2026. Unit 1 (60 kL) inaugurated 3-Jun-2026, qualification from Nov-2026, validation batches in 2027, steady revenue from calendar 2028. Unit 2 (60 kL drug substance, US$150-180mn capex) construction from Oct-2026, revenue from 2031. Target US$150-200mn of revenue from 2032 at 35-50% EBITDA margin.
theranym.src: Q4FY26 and Q1FY27 presentations and calls

governance.board: Nine directors at Mar-2026: two executive, seven non-executive including four independent (one woman); non-executive independent chairman since the LIC veteran joined

history.event: Founded in Hyderabad by P.V. Ramprasad Reddy and K. Nithyananda Reddy; semi-synthetic penicillin APIs; IPO in 1992
Bought US formulations facilities (AuroLife) and Milpharm (UK); US generics build-out begins
Acquired Actavis's commercial operations in seven Western European countries
Generis (Portugal); Apotex's businesses in five European countries; seven branded oncology injectables from Spectrum (Acrotech)
Sold Natrol (US nutraceuticals): Rs2,815 cr exceptional gain
US price erosion and Eugia compliance problems: EBITDA margin falls to ~15% in FY23; India entry via Veritaz

gRevlimid sales and new launches: margin back to 20-21%; Pen-G PLI plant built; GLS Pharma (51%, then 100%); MSD biologics CMO deal (May-2024); Rs750 cr buyback (Jul-2024); Eugia Unit III warning letter (Aug-2024)
Zentiva bid lost to GTCR (Sep-2025); Lannett agreed (Jul-2025); first EU biosimilar approvals
gRevlimid fades; Europe passes EUR1bn; Khandelwal brands (Jan-2026); MIP on Pen-G (Jan-2026); Pen-G turns EBITDA positive (Q4)
Rs800 cr buyback (Apr-May); Eugia Unit I and III OAI; Lannett closed (29-Jun); TheraNym Unit 1 inaugurated (3-Jun); A1 Biochem agreed (Jul); Eugia Unit I warning letter (13-Aug)
